## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

run-name: "OpenCode #${{ github.event.issue.number || inputs.issue_number }}${{ github.event.issue.title && format(' — {0}', github.event.issue.title) || '' }}"

on:
  issues:
    types: [opened]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue_number:
        description: Existing issue to run
        required: true
        type: string

permissions: {}

concurrency:
  group: opencode-issue-${{ github.repository }}-${{ github.event.issue.number || inputs.issue_number }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  prepare:
    if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' || (github.event.action == 'opened' && contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'OpenCode'))
    permissions:
      contents: write
      id-token: write
      issues: write
      actions: write
    uses: denaidark/OhMyGithub/.github/workflows/opencode-prepare.yml@3b460fef6b0cbee61ae301726c8a54b00b73bfd2
    with:
      runtime_ref: 3b460fef6b0cbee61ae301726c8a54b00b73bfd2

  opencode:
    needs: prepare
    if: needs.prepare.outputs.approved == 'true'
    permissions:
      contents: write
      id-token: write
      issues: write
      actions: read
      pull-requests: write
    uses: denaidark/OhMyGithub/.github/workflows/opencode-reusable.yml@3b460fef6b0cbee61ae301726c8a54b00b73bfd2
    with:
      runtime_ref: 3b460fef6b0cbee61ae301726c8a54b00b73bfd2
      issue_number: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.issue_number }}
      request: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.request }}
      issue_title: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.issue_title }}
      labels_json: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.labels_json }}
      sender: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.sender }}
      target_ref: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.target_ref }}
      target_sha: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.target_sha }}
    secrets:
      OPENCODE_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENCODE_API_KEY }}
      OPENCODE_AUTH_JSON: ${{ secrets.OPENCODE_AUTH_JSON }}
      AGENTSWEB_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY: ${{ secrets.AGENTSWEB_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY }}

# 🤯 OMG — Oh My GitHub ### 🚀 One Prompt In. A Full Game or App Out. 🚀 [![Status](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-🔥%20works-brightgreen?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/actions) [![GitHub Issues](https://img.shields.io/github/issues/denaidark/OhMyGithub?style=for-the-badge&logo=github)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/issues) [![GitHub Actions](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub%20Actions-automated-2088FF?style=for-the-badge&logo=githubactions&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/actions) [![OpenCode](https://img.shields.io/badge/powered%20by-OpenCode-111111?style=for-the-badge)](https://opencode.ai/) ```text ╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗ ║ DESCRIBE IT → BUILD IT → TEST IT → PLAY IT ║ ║ ║ ║ One GitHub issue. One prompt. A complete project. ║ ╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝ ``` **No API keys to configure. No server to maintain. No local setup maze.**
--- ## 🤯 What Is OMG? > **Your GitHub issue becomes the product brief.** OMG (Oh My GitHub) is an automated GitHub Actions workflow for creating complete browser games and app projects from one natural-language prompt. Write what you want in an issue and add the `OpenCode` label. OpenCode checks out the project, uses the shared skills, builds the experience, runs tests, verifies the result, and publishes an immutable OmGithub project link from the finished commit. Yes, it creates the code. Yes, it runs the verification loop. Yes, it can expose the result in a temporary browser URL. ## 🧠 TL;DR 1. Open a GitHub issue. 2. Describe the game or app you want. 3. Add the `OpenCode` label to the issue. 4. Let GitHub Actions build, test, verify, and propose the result. ```text Your idea → GitHub issue → OpenCode → tests → immutable OmGithub project ``` ## ⚡ Quick Start Create an issue in your repository with a concrete request: ```text Build a neon asteroid game. Requirements: - Arrow-key movement - Score and restart button - Win and lose states - Responsive browser layout - Run tests and verify it in a browser ``` That is the whole user-facing workflow. GitHub Actions handles the runner, OpenCode handles implementation, and the workflow handles verification plus the immutable project commit. To run against an existing non-default branch, end the issue title with a `branch: ` directive. The directive selects the checkout and is removed before the issue body is sent to OpenCode: ```sh gh issue create \ --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub \ --title "Custom branch smoke test branch: codex/omgithub-site" \ --body "Build a tiny browser page." \ --label Goal \ --label OpenCode ``` The GitHub App validates the branch before dispatching. If the directive is absent, the repository default branch remains the target. ## 🌍 What Can You Build? | 🎯 Use case | ✨ Example | |---|---| | 🎮 Arcade games | Breakout, Space Invaders, Asteroids, Match-3 | | 🧩 Puzzle games | Word games, logic puzzles, card games | | 🏃 Interactive demos | Physics experiments, simulations, visual toys | | 📊 Dashboards | Filters, charts, status panels, analytics views | | 🛠️ Internal tools | Trackers, generators, small workflow apps | | 🌐 Landing pages | Product pages, portfolios, interactive showcases | | 🧪 Prototypes | Turn a product idea into a runnable proof of concept | | 📱 Browser apps | Responsive tools that work on desktop and mobile | ## 🧰 What Happens Automatically? > **The workflow is the product.** - 📥 Checks out your repository and the shared OpenCode skills. - 🏷️ Synchronizes `model/*` and `skill/*` labels. - 🧭 Reads issue labels to select the model and requested skills. - 🤖 Runs OpenCode against the current project. - 🧪 Runs a second verification prompt after implementation. - 🌐 Starts the app and checks the local runtime. - 🔗 Creates a temporary public preview URL when verification passes. - 🔀 Creates and pushes an `opencode/` branch. - 🕹️ Adds an `Open Project` link backed by the repository path, with full-commit links retained for compatibility. - 💬 Posts progress and access details back to the issue. - 🧹 Cleans up temporary tunnels and runner processes. ## 🏷️ Model and Skill Labels Labels let you control the workflow without editing YAML. ```text model/opencode/deepseek-v4.1-flash-free skill/load-sketchfab-threejs skill/gauntlet-loop ``` The workflow validates the selected labels, passes them into OpenCode, and records the resolved model and skills in the run logs. Shared skills are discovered from: ```text .agents/skills//SKILL.md ``` ## 🔄 OpenCode Workflow ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Trigger] --> B[Prepare project] B --> C[Run build.md] C --> D[Run verify.md] D --> E{Public app works?} E -- No --> F[Run public-app-fix.md] F --> E E -- Yes --> G[Run completion-report.md] G --> H{Screenshots exist?} H -- No --> I[Run screenshot-evidence.md] I --> H H -- Yes --> J[Commit and push] J --> K[Create immutable project link] K --> L[Publish report] L --> M[Complete] ``` ## 🏗️ Architecture === # OMG (Oh My GitHub) agent instructions Do not implement, suggest, report, or propose security issues unless the user explicitly asks for a security review. Inspect the OpenCode implementation at `/Users/igor/Documents/ChatGPT/opencode` and [anomalyco/opencode](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode) for related requests. ## Wiki index - [OpenCode workflow](wiki/opencode.md) - [Test OpenCode execution](wiki/opencode-v2-experiment.md) - [Oh My Github App](https://github.com/denaidark/omsite/blob/main/wiki/oh-my-github-app.md) - [Temporary Mac SSH access](wiki/access.md) - [Testing and verification](wiki/testing.md) - [OmGithub publishing](https://github.com/denaidark/omsite/blob/main/wiki/omgithub.md) ## Main project file The main project file is [.github/workflows/opencode.yml](.github/workflows/opencode.yml). Keep the local [game issue E2E skill](.agents/skills/game-issue-e2e/SKILL.md) aligned with this workflow. Create an issue with `OpenCode` and only user-requested mode labels already attached, to start the native `issues.opened` listener. Wait only for the initial OpenCode session link during E2E kickoff. Install the listener on the default branch before requesting execution. Validate author access and freeze the request inside Actions before starting the reusable execution job. Set repository variable `OPENCODE_ACCESS=everyone` to accept any issue author for labeled issues. Keep the App as a setup helper. Use Actions concurrency to serialize each issue. Store `branch` in an `omgithub-request:v1` JSON HTML comment to select the project checkout, result base, and workflow. Let default-branch preparation dispatch the selected branch. Run preparation and OpenCode in that branch run. ## Shell timing When writing shell scripts, always add explicit per-command execution-time measurements between commands. Use `/usr/bin/time -p` or a small timing helper around each meaningful command; the outer command duration is not sufficient because it hides which step is slow or hung. Use `/usr/bin/time` only in scripts; do not invoke it directly in interactive shell commands. ## Ideas Store durable implementation ideas as individual Markdown files under `./ideas/`, using descriptive kebab-case filenames such as `ideas/opencode-oauth-env-auth.md`. ## Links in handoffs When a relevant URL or stable identifier exists, include a clickable Markdown link in the user-facing response. Link GitHub issues, Actions runs, pull requests, commits, releases, public app URLs, and Codex tasks/threads rather than reporting only their numbers or plain text. For Codex tasks/threads, use the `codex://threads/` URL format. When mentioning a commit, append its relative age in hours or days. ## OpenCode GitHub Actions To execute an issue, create it with `OpenCode` and only mode labels explicitly requested by the user. Check for a native `issues` run and successful preparation. The workflow starts a temporary AgentsWeb SSH session, verifies it, runs OpenCode, and cleans up the SSH session afterward. When monitoring a triggered run, use `gh run watch --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub --exit-status` for overall job status. Do not use `gh run view --log` to read logs from a running task: GitHub reports that logs are unavailable until completion. Use `bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh ` for the live Actions log over SSH. Do not use tight `for` loops around `gh run list`, which needlessly consume GitHub API rate limit. Free OpenCode models are limited per egress IP, not per account. Treat a local `FreeUsageLimitError` 429 as local only. Read the runner's own `Selected model` and provider errors before blaming quota. Use `retryAfterMs` as the reset bound. Run repeated V2 tests with a connected provider; do not spend the free allowance on retries. Interrupting a V2 turn before the assistant message projects leaves no stopped message to save. Wait for that assistant message before requiring the interrupted idle marker. To connect to an issue's live worker, find its run ID with `gh run list --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub --workflow opencode.yml --status in_progress`, then run `bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh ` to discover the host and port and SSH with `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb` as shown by the helper. When the user asks to check a live OpenCode workflow, always pull the runner logs over SSH first, using `scripts/ssh-run-log.sh` or a targeted SSH read from the same runner. Base the answer on those logs before discussing whether an action is confirmed; do not lead with a generic inability-to-confirm statement when live log evidence can be collected. For real-time inspection from a live temporary SSH session, use the helper: ```sh bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh ``` The helper discovers the temporary SSH command from the triggering issue or pull request, then follows the freshest `_diag/pages` log. The runner uploads chunks from `_diag/blocks` to GitHub. Do not print environment files, tokens, or private keys while inspecting the runner. ## Mac SSH access The Mac private key stays at `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb`. Its public key is stored in the repository Actions secret `AGENTSWEB_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY`. The issue commented by the workflow contains a directly usable command such as: ```sh ssh -i ~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb -p runner@.agentsweb.space ``` The command works only while the corresponding Actions job is running. ## Connecting to a live OpenCode worker Use the repository helper to discover the worker host and port from the broker or issue comment. It uses the persistent local key `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb`: ```sh bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub ``` For an interactive shell, reuse the host and port printed by the helper and use the same key: ```sh ssh -tt -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no \ -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null \ -i ~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb \ -p runner@.agentsweb.space ``` Do not substitute the generated runner key under `sshworker/outputs/keys/`; it can produce a misleading `Permission denied (publickey)` result. Temporary worker SSH access ends when the Actions job and session are cleaned up. Never print secrets while inspecting a worker.

playwright-cli - run playwright mcp commands from terminal

Usage: playwright-cli <command> [args] [options]
Usage: playwright-cli -s=<session> <command> [args] [options]

Core:
  open [url]                  open the browser
  attach [name]               attach to a running playwright browser
  close                       close the browser
  detach                      detach from an attached browser
  goto <url>                  navigate to a url
  type <text>                 type text into editable element
  click <target> [button]     perform click on a web page
  dblclick <target> [button]  perform double click on a web page
  fill <target> <text>        fill text into editable element
  drag <startTarget> <endTarget> perform drag and drop between two elements
  drop <target>               drop files or data onto an element
  hover <target>              hover over element on page
  select <target> <val>       select an option in a dropdown
  upload <files...>           upload one or multiple files
  check <target>              check a checkbox or radio button
  uncheck <target>            uncheck a checkbox or radio button
  snapshot [target]           capture page snapshot to obtain element ref
  find [text]                 search the page snapshot for text or a regexp, returning matching nodes with surrounding context (like search snippets)
  eval <func> [target]        evaluate javascript expression on page or element
  dialog-accept [prompt]      accept a dialog
  dialog-dismiss              dismiss a dialog
  resize <w> <h>              resize the browser window
  delete-data                 delete session data

Navigation:
  go-back                     go back to the previous page
  go-forward                  go forward to the next page
  reload                      reload the current page

Keyboard:
  press <key>                 press a key on the keyboard, `a`, `arrowleft`
  keydown <key>               press a key down on the keyboard
  keyup <key>                 press a key up on the keyboard

Mouse:
  mousemove <x> <y>           move mouse to a given position
  mousedown [button]          press mouse down
  mouseup [button]            press mouse up
  mousewheel <dx> <dy>        scroll mouse wheel

Save as:
  screenshot [target]         screenshot of the current page or element
  pdf                         save page as pdf

Tabs:
  tab-list                    list all tabs
  tab-new [url]               create a new tab
  tab-close [index]           close a browser tab
  tab-select <index>          select a browser tab

Storage:
  state-load <filename>       loads browser storage (authentication) state from a file
  state-save [filename]       saves the current storage (authentication) state to a file
  cookie-list                 list all cookies (optionally filtered by domain/path)

```js
drawRidge(baseY, amp, freq, parallax, color, t, jagged, glowColor) {
  const offset = cam.x * parallax;
  ctx.beginPath();
  ctx.moveTo(-50, viewH+50);
  const step=48;
  for(let sx=-50; sx<=viewW+50; sx+=step){
    const wx = sx + offset;
    let y = baseY + Math.sin(wx*freq)*amp + Math.sin(wx*freq*2.7+1.5)*amp*0.35;
    if(jagged) y += (hash(Math.floor(wx/step))-0.5)*amp*1.1;
    ctx.lineTo(sx,y);
  }
  ctx.lineTo(viewW+50, viewH+50); close; fill.
}
```

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build "PORTAL RUNNER – Dimension Adventure", a visually stunning 2D browser platformer with two worlds, functional portal dimension switching, jumping/dashing, hidden collectibles, moving platforms, environmental puzzles, animated transitions, five levels, character animation, mobile + keyboard controls, progression and localStorage save.

## Requirements
- Two visually different worlds with dimension switching that affects actual gameplay.
- Platform jumping, dashing, hidden collectibles/secret paths, moving platforms, environmental puzzles.
- Animated portals and dimension transition effects.
- Five progressively challenging levels, beautiful backgrounds, animated character.
- Mobile and keyboard controls; every button and feature functional.
- Level progression and save system.
- Must be verified in a real browser with screenshots and interaction tests.

## Decisions
- Static HTML/CSS/vanilla JS Canvas 2D game (no build step), served by provided static server via `index.html`.
- Two layers per level: `light` ("Lumen") and `dark` ("Umbra"); layer-exclusive platforms/walls/hazards, lower gravity and lava in dark.
- Portal interaction via `E`/`F`/`Enter` or mobile `PHASE`, not auto-switch; linked secret portals teleport to hidden areas.
- Player abilities: run, variable jump, double jump, one air dash, coyote time, jump buffering.
- Puzzles: glyph plates toggle energy bridges in the opposite dimension; crumbling platforms.
- Progression: 5 levels, 3 keys each, shards; stars = complete + ≥75% shards + all keys; sequential unlock.
- Save key `portal-runner-save-v1` with levels, best shards/keys/time/stars, settings.
- Procedural art/audio only (no external assets); Web Audio generative music and synthesized SFX.
- Verification planned with `playwright-cli`, screenshots, and `window.__portalRunner` debug hooks.

## Work State
### Completed
- `index.html`: full UI shell (title, level select, help, settings, pause, complete, HUD, touch controls, transition/vignette/flash layers).
- `styles.css`: full responsive glass UI, logo, buttons, level cards, settings, dialogs, stars, mobile joystick/buttons, reduced-motion styles.
- `js/levels.js`: five hand-authored levels, both layers, palettes, shared + exclusive solids, hazards, moving platforms, plates/bridges, enemies, shards, keys, portals (including linked secret portals), checkpoints, tips, goals, normalization helpers.
- `js/audio.js`: AudioEngine with generative pads/arpeggios/reverb and synthesized SFX.
- `js/save.js`: load/write/default save, star calculation, `recordLevel`, reset, progress summary, `formatTime`.
- `js/utils.js`: math/hash/color helpers.
- `js/game.js`: core engine — state flow, input, fixed-step physics/collision, moving/crumbling platforms, plate/bridge logic, collectibles, hazards, enemies/stomp/dash kills, portals/teleport/transition, death/respawn/checkpoints, camera, particles, completion, debug hooks.
- `js/ui.js`: screen navigation, dynamic level cards, HUD updates, prompt/toast/banner, pause/complete, settings sync/toggles, reset confirmation, touch joystick and buttons.
- `js/world.js`: full world renderer — ghost other-layer geometry, platforms/monoliths, crumble/moving platforms, lava/spikes, bridges, plates, checkpoints, animated portals/goal arch, shards/keys, watcher enemies, high-detail player with cape/scarf/visor/dash ghosts, particles, floating text.
- Wall heights adjusted so dark-layer barriers are not bypassable by high dark-gravity jumps.
- Bridge data corrected so each bridge exists only in its intended layer; Level 3 extra key/plate removed.

### Active
- `js/renderer.js` is still missing; it must provide `Renderer` with `render(t)` and `makeCardArt(level)`.
- `js/main.js` is still missing; must boot `new Game()` and expose `window.__portalRunner = game`.
- Need first syntax/runtime validation, then browser testing and screenshots.

### Blocked
- Nothing external; game cannot launch until renderer/main exist.

## Next Move
1. Create `js/renderer.js` importing `drawWorldScene` from `world.js`; implement screen transform (`dpr * view.scale`), animated menu attract scene, sky/parallax background, dimension flash DOM updates, and `makeCardArt(level)`.
2. Create `js/main.js` with `new Game()` and `window.__portalRunner`.
3. Run `node --check` on all JS files and fix errors.
4. Start static server (use project start mechanism or `python3 -m http.server 3002`) and open with `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002`.
5. Verify title screen/menu buttons, start level 1, movement/jump/dash/portal switch via Playwright; exercise debug hooks and complete a level; inspect screenshots and fix visual/logic issues.
6. Inspect desktop + mobile viewport screenshots; verify no console errors; confirm level select, settings, pause, complete, reset, touch controls.
7. Final polish pass on visuals/transitions/audio and ensure every button works.

## Relevant Files
- `js/renderer.js`: missing orchestrator renderer; highest priority.
- `js/main.js`: missing entry point.
- `js/game.js`: engine; UI expects `game.renderer.makeCardArt(level)` and debug hooks.
- `js/world.js`: world/player rendering; exports `drawWorldScene(r, game, t)`.
- `js/ui.js`: all DOM behavior and screen navigation.
- `js/levels.js`: level data and normalization.
- `js/save.js`: save/progress logic.
- `js/audio.js`: music/SFX.
- `js/utils.js`: shared helpers.
- `index.html`: DOM ids/classes and screens.
- `styles.css`: UI and mobile styling.
- `start.sh` / runtime `default-start.mjs`: serves static `index.html` on port from `PORT` (default 3000).

## Important Context
- Renderer contract expected by Game/UI: `new Renderer(game)`; `render(t)`; `makeCardArt(level)` returns data URL. Uses `game.ctx`, `game.view {w,h,scale,cw,ch,dpr}`, `game.cam {x,y,shake}`, `game.level`, `game.layer`, `game.particles`, `game.effects`, `game.speedLines`, `game.ghosts`, `game.floaters`, `game.interaction`, `game.dimFlash`, `game.dimFlashPos`.
- Game loop calls `renderer.render(this.t)` then `ui.updateHUD(this)`.
- `Game` constructor already calls `new Renderer(this)` and `new UI(this)` in that order; missing module will currently break import.
- Renderer should set `#flash` opacity/position from `dimFlash`/`dimFlashPos` (element available via `game.ui.el.flash`).
- `game.mode` values: `title`, `levels`, `help`, `settings`, `playing`, `paused`, `complete`; `ui.screen` tracks visible screen.
- Debug hooks: `window.__portalRunner.debugState()`, `.debugTeleport(x, y, layer)`, `.debugCollectAll()`, `.startLevel(index)`, `.completeLevel()`.
- Level ground top is y=640; view base height 720 desktop/640 touch; portrait ensures min view width 560.
- `playwright-cli` available; `~/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` uses headed Chromium + Xvfb.
- Work is uncommitted in `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround`.
- A potential UI issue noted: `showPause()`/`showComplete()` should use `showOnly(...)` to clear other active screens when returning from settings.
- `prompt` hides via removing `.show` but leaves `.hidden` removed; cosmetic only.
- Level 1 secret portal pair: light `(2080,640)` ↔ dark `(2080,300)`; portals at `1460`, `2960`, `3540`; walls at light `3080` and dark `3740`; goal `4250,640`.
